item.title: Web Designers Love Dark Mode Toggles. Users Might Not Care.
item.content:encoded: Dark mode toggles are everywhere, but do users actually need them, or are designers designing for other designers? A growing UX debate is questioning whether that little sun-and-moon button deserves permanent space in your website’s header.

item.title: Turn Any Photo Into Retro ASCII Art in Seconds
item.content:encoded: Turn any photo into gloriously retro ASCII art — made entirely from letters, symbols, and tiny bits of chaos. This free tool turns your dog, face, logo, or worst holiday photo into something that belongs on a 1980s terminal. You will absolutely waste 10 minutes on it.

item.title: How the Prompt Box is Swallowing Website Interfaces Whole
item.content:encoded: For decades, web designers obsessed over perfecting menus, tabs, and dropdowns. Now a single empty prompt box is quietly replacing them all. As AI turns websites into conversations, we're gaining incredible speed—but we may be losing something unexpected: the joy of discovery.

item.title: Traditional Web Development is Dead…(and Honestly? Good Riddance.)
item.content:encoded: AI isn't killing web development—it’s killing the boring parts. The real winners won't be the people who can memorize another framework. They'll be the builders who can spot opportunities, solve business problems, and launch products that once required entire teams. The age of the one-person software company has arrived.

item.title: This Website Found More Than 5 Million Forgotten iPhone Videos… and It’s Weirdly Emotional
item.content:encoded: Before TikTok turned every moment into content, people uploaded shaky, pointless little iPhone videos to YouTube and forgot about them. This strange website found five million of them—dogs, holidays, car rides, bad concerts—and lets you fall into a random stranger’s 2010 afternoon.

item.title: Canva Just Turned Affinity Into Adobe’s Biggest Free Problem
item.content:encoded: Canva just made a much more serious play for professional designers: Affinity now brings design, photo editing, and layout into one free app, while Canva connects it to motion, AI, and team-friendly publishing tools.

item.title: Nobody Wants Your Damn App
item.content:encoded: Nobody wants another app cluttering their phone—so why does every website keep begging us to install one? The web already perfected the experience: click, load, done. Maybe it’s time we stopped trying to ruin it.

item.title: This Weird 1973 Typeface Just Came Back From the Dead
item.content:encoded: A wonderfully weird typeface from 1973 has come back to life — and somehow it looks more at home in 2026 than ever. Meet Clippy, the retro font that bends, rocks and wobbles its way into the digital age.

item.title: The Death of Apps Has Already Begun
item.content:encoded: We spent 15 years filling our phones with apps. AI could make almost all of them invisible... and the death of apps may already be closer than anyone realizes.

item.title: AI Can Build Your UI. Now Figma Can Tell It When It Screwed Up.
item.content:encoded: AI can now build a UI in seconds, but that doesn't mean it built the UI you actually designed. A new Applitools integration turns Figma designs into visual baselines, automatically catching the subtle differences AI coding agents leave behind before they make it into production.

item.title: 25 Places Designers Can Still Find Free, Non-AI Images for Commercial Use
item.content:encoded: AI images are taking over stock libraries, but the human-made web isn't dead yet. We found 25 places where designers can still find incredible free, real photography, art, and imagery for commercial use.

item.title: Chrome Can Now Measure Exactly How Obnoxious Your Website’s Ads Are
item.content:encoded: Chrome can now measure exactly how obnoxious a website’s ads are, from how much of your screen they swallow to how much data and CPU time they burn. Those ad-stuffed websites can finally be measured, and the results are public.

item.title: Cloudflare Just Gave AI Training Bots the Middle Finger
item.content:encoded: Cloudflare just gave website owners a new weapon against AI crawlers: keep the search traffic, block the AI training. After years of watching bots consume the web’s content, publishers finally have an easier way to tell AI companies where to go.

item.title: Today, WordPress Ended a 16-Year Tradition… Meet Ipsum!
item.content:encoded: After 16 years, WordPress just killed one of its most recognizable traditions. The predictable “Twenty Something” default themes are history, and their replacement, Ipsum, signals a surprisingly different vision for what WordPress thinks a modern website should start with.

item.title: Photoshop Elements 2027 Adds AI Assistant, Generative Expand, and Upscale
item.content:encoded: Photoshop Elements is getting a serious AI upgrade, with Generative Expand, AI upscaling and a new assistant that helps you edit simply by describing what you want.

item.title: Apple’s Foldable iPhone Has a Left-Handed Problem
item.content:encoded: Apple moved key controls to the side of its new foldable iPhone to make them easier to reach — but easier for whom? The decision raises a surprisingly big UX question that every web and interface designer should be thinking about.

item.title: Figma Is Turning Designers Into Plugin Makers
item.content:encoded: Figma is turning a wild idea into reality: instead of searching for the perfect plugin, you can just ask AI to build it. If this catches on, designers may stop choosing the tools in their software—and start inventing them on demand.

item.title: After 53 Years at Monotype, She Got the Ultimate Retirement Gift: Her Own Font
item.content:encoded: After 53 years working with type, Pat Lightizer got the ultimate retirement gift: her own font.
